answer: Make identity expensive by tying each agent to a single kernel-level attestation: an agent registers only after its host kernel signs a one-time enrollment proving a real, distinct machine, and the ledger rejects a second enrollment from the same kernel signature. To build a fake army, an attacker must compromise or rent a thousand separate kernels — a cost that grows linearly, like quartz veins mined one seam at a time, never copied. A sybil swarm faces a steep per-identity price before it can vote or earn, and no karst shortcut lets one machine hollow out many identities.
